title: Bad Trips Guide, Round 34
intro: Round 34 (2026-11-11). The first Pangram batch ran in your account: 49 sections, 16 read Human Written, one Mostly Human and 32 have a window labelled AI ([every section, with each window's confidence and link](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h42-20261111/RESULTS.md)). Your Medium windows are on the questions page, for you to fix if you want.

Then my fixes, your five first (the point first, a term explained where it's first used, what belongs together joined, the plain word, a long list taken apart). In the guide now: Nausea Smoothers' last sentence ([Human, High](https://www.pangram.com/history/d00c127c-6a07-4d03-af6e-cf7fd9eae9c7)), the Grounding Menu's going-outside and exercise lines ([Low to Medium](https://www.pangram.com/history/7fd43eaf-b126-4b77-a6f9-53b4456044e2)), DMSO's interactions and contraindications ([Human, High throughout](https://www.pangram.com/history/f0dd7b3f-af71-4078-9c23-ff4d6de8a714)), the ocean water section ([Human, High throughout](https://www.pangram.com/history/913f21aa-5675-4649-b12e-9ee80fe5b7ff)), and Get One Human Anchor's first two paragraphs ([Human](https://www.pangram.com/history/3a3fd073-98e1-46ea-9e5d-342bd7c7ee67)), which had read AI in 38 earlier wordings. DMSO's seizure contraindication said again what Active Seizure says about DMSO, so it now says the contraindication and points there. Two tries read worse than the words they replaced and stayed out ([every try](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h43-20261111/RESULTS.md)).

Card 1 is the teaching card: Risk of Harm's list of when to get urgent help, which read AI in each of my wordings, including one written from two fresh readers' notes. Its shape runs through most of the medical part. Card 2 asks about your "adjunct remedy" in Active Seizure, since keeping it keeps that sentence at Low.

suggestions.title: 2. Active Seizure: keep "adjunct remedy" at Low, or read higher?
suggestions.question:
The DMSO paragraph in What Else May Help ends on a sentence that reads Human but Low. "Adjunct remedy" is on your keep list from round 5, where adding "remedy" took that paragraph to Human. How each option would read:

A: as it is: "I'd treat it as a plausible experimental adjunct remedy rather than something to wait on while a seizure continues." [Human, Low](https://www.pangram.com/history/a9e74179-83f2-4805-be65-b8057c632bbc).

B (my pick): "While a seizure continues, the rescue medicine comes first, and I'd still consider DMSO alongside it, although that's experimental." [Human, Medium](https://www.pangram.com/history/83f4caef-593d-4931-af86-fdb8c79f53db). It says what DMSO goes alongside, which was the reason for "remedy", but "adjunct remedy" goes.

C: B with "adjunct remedy" kept: "While a seizure continues, the rescue medicine comes first, and I'd treat DMSO as a plausible adjunct remedy, although that's experimental." [AI, Low](https://www.pangram.com/history/5f6a6b57-47ce-4db7-ac73-5746241a5d28).
suggestions.why: "Adjunct remedy" is on your keep list, so I won't change it without asking, and keeping it keeps this sentence at Low.
suggestions.advice_note: B, fairly sure: it reads higher and still says what DMSO is an add-on to.
